user_filter_interpretation.evidence: Official search API distinguishes cpu_cores (virtual CPUs) from cpu_cores_effective.
user_filter_interpretation.assessment: 98 is a severe and probably unnecessary single-GPU filter for the measured small GRU; it can hide useful one-GPU offers. Indexed cards display A40 allocations of 20/40 or 64/256 CPU, an A100 PCIe at 8/16 CPU, and an H100 PCIe at 32/256 CPU. If the URL maps to per-offer virtual CPU as the API's cpu_cores field suggests, 98 would exclude all these cards; confirm the UI-to-API mapping and compare effective vCPUs and measured input throughput after authentication.

user_filter_interpretation.evidence: Official API describes cpu_ghz in GHz.
user_filter_interpretation.assessment: This cutoff is extremely low and likely removes very little. The URL is a console state; its precise parser behavior was not accessible.

user_filter_interpretation.evidence: Official API exposes separate inet_up, inet_down, and transfer-cost fields; the UI parameter's exact conversion was not documented in retrieved sources.
user_filter_interpretation.assessment: May constrain host egress while initial dataset staging needs the reverse direction. Measure both. If it means sustained decimal Mbit/s, 208 Mbit/s is 26 MB/s and 34.86 GB takes at least 22.35 minutes one way before protocol, cache, hashing, or decompression.

user_filter_interpretation.evidence: Closest documented API field is dph_total, described as total dollars per hour.
user_filter_interpretation.assessment: A ceiling, not a live price or recommendation. Multiplying by 7197 seconds gives about $6.45 before any separately billed disk/network items or setup and cleanup delay.

user_filter_interpretation.evidence: Official search API documents reliability as a score in [0,1].
user_filter_interpretation.assessment: Permissive score threshold relative to the selected detailed public-index snapshots (their listed scores range from 98.0% to 99.916%), but this nonrandom, stale sample does not characterize the market. The docs do not define it as a job-completion probability; do not use 0.617 as a per-run success prior.

user_filter_interpretation.evidence: Official API documents duration as minimum offer availability in seconds.
user_filter_interpretation.assessment: About two hours of availability, not a guaranteed end-to-end job deadline. Account for cold start, data movement, profiling, fit, export, download, and cleanup.

user_filter_interpretation.evidence: Official API has an explicit verified filter for machine verification.
user_filter_interpretation.assessment: A false UI toggle may disable that filter instead of requesting unverified hosts. Do not infer its truth table from the URL; query verified and relaxed cohorts explicitly after authentication works.

user_filter_interpretation.evidence: The retrieved search API exposes driver_version and compute_cap but no matching compatibility flag.
user_filter_interpretation.assessment: False is not evidence that an offer is incompatible. Validate CUDA, PyTorch, cuDNN, device visibility, and the actual recurrent kernel in a bounded profile.

arithmetic_derived_from_user_filters_not.historical_projection_limit: Different GRU128 two-seed recipe; old profile estimated fit/export before refusing a frozen 6300-second cap. It is not an H230 estimate, current offer quote, or completion-time guarantee.
arithmetic_derived_from_user_filters_not.status: scenario arithmetic only; no offer, quote, transfer measurement, or success probability
arithmetic_derived_from_user_filters_not.budget_arithmetic_limit: At the URL ceiling the reported $20 balance represents about 6.20 billed hours before any nonincluded bandwidth or other cost. Three 7,197-second windows at that ceiling cost about $19.35, leaving about $0.65; this is scenario arithmetic only, not a recommendation, quote, or guarantee that an offer/job runs that long.

sequence: Query current balance, auto-top-up state, current instances, and account-wide active spend.
Search one-GPU on-demand verified/rentable capacity across a small GPU-family matrix; start with relaxed CPU filters and a price ceiling derived from the current remaining credit.

Query interruptible/bid offers as a separate cohort only after exact checkpoint/resume has passed; do not treat the advertised discount as a completion-rate prior. Avoid reserved terms for the short profile unless their actual upfront cost and term are favorable.
Repeat with one filter relaxed at a time to detect which saved UI filters remove otherwise compatible offers.
Save the raw response in the private authorized workspace and a redacted projection with timestamp, query, row count, offer identifiers, host identity hash, and all cost/compatibility fields.
Make no instance-creation call during market discovery.
